source_text: Σοφία δὲ ἐν ἀνθρώπῳ ἐξεταζομένη, καὶ διὰ προσώπου φαίνεται φωτίζουσα τὸν κεκτημένον· ὥσπερ οὖν ἀναίδεια, μίσους εὐθὺς ὀφθέντα ἄξιον ἐκεῖνον ἐλέγχει, ᾧπερ ἐνῴκησε. Πάνυ δὲ χρὴ ἐπιμελῶς τοῖς τοῦ βασιλέως προσέχειν λόγοις, ὅρκον δὲ ἐκ παντὸς τρόπου φεύγειν, μάλιστα τὸν εἰς Θεοῦ ὄνομα γινόμενον. Ἐφίστασθαι δὲ ὅμως προσήκει λόγῳ πονηρῷ· ἀλλὰ φυλάσσεσθαι ἅπασαν τὴν εἰς τὸν Δεσπότην βλασφημίαν. Οὐ γὰρ δὴ ἐπάγοντός τι μέμφεσθαι ὑπάρξει, οὐδὲ ἀντιλέγειν τοῖς τοῦ μόνου δυνάστου καὶ βασιλέως δόγμασι. Βέλτιον δὲ, καὶ λυσιτελέστερον ἐμμένοντα ταῖς ἱεραῖς ἐντολαῖς, λόγων τῶν πονηρῶν ἐκτὸς καθεστάναι. Σοφὸς γὰρ ἀνὴρ ἐπίσταται καὶ προγινώσκει τὴν εἰς καιρὸν κρίσιν, ὅτι δικαία ἔσται. Πάντα γὰρ τὰ ἐν τῷ βίῳ τῶν ἀνθρώπων πράγματα περιμένει τὴν ἄνωθεν κόλασιν· πλὴν ὅ γε πονηρὸς, οὐ λίαν γινώσκειν ἔοικεν, ὅτι πολλῆς ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ οὔσης προνοίας, οὐδὲν ὁτιοῦν εἰς τὸ μετέπειτα λήσεται. Οὐ γὰρ οἶδε τὰ ἐπιόντα· οὐδὲν γὰρ αὐτῶν κατ᾽ ἀξίαν τις ἀναγγεῖλαι δυνήσεται· ὅτι οὐχ οὕτως τις ἰσχυρὸς ὑπάρξει, ὡς τὸν ἀφαιρούμενον τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἄγγελον κωλῦσαι δύνασθαι, οὐδέ τις ὅλως μέθοδος εὑρεθείη ἂν τοῦ παραγράφασθαί πως τὸν καιρὸν τῆς τελευτῆς· ἀλλ᾽ ὥσπερ ἐν πολέμῳ μέσῳ ληφθέντα, ἄφυκτα πανταχόθεν ἔστιν ὁρᾷν, ἀσέβεια δὲ πᾶσα ἀνθρώπου συνεξόλλυται.
thought_title: Wisdom, the king's word, and the hour of death
orientation: Wisdom shines in the face; one must heed the king's word and avoid oaths, for no one can escape the hour of death.
pass_a_gloss: Wisdom examined in a man appears even through the face, illuminating its possessor; just as then shamelessness at once refutes that one, being seen, worthy of hatred, in whom it dwelt. One must very carefully attend to the words of the king, and flee an oath in every way, especially the one made into God's name. Yet it is fitting to attend to/stand over an evil word; but to guard against all blasphemy toward the Master. For, he bringing on something, it will not be [possible] to blame, nor to speak against the decrees of the only Ruler and King. Better and more profitable, abiding in the holy commandments, to stand outside evil words. For a wise man knows and foreknows the judgment in season, that it will be just. For all affairs in the life of men await the punishment from above; except the wicked one does not seem to know very well that, there being much providence over him, nothing whatever will escape notice hereafter. For he does not know the things coming; for no one will be able to announce any of them worthily; because no one will be so strong as to be able to hinder the angel taking away his soul, nor would any method at all be found to set aside by plea the time of death; but as one caught in the midst of war, it is [possible] to see inescapable things from all sides, and all ungodliness of man perishes with [him].

pass_b_english: When wisdom is tested in a person, it shines out even through the face, lighting up the one who possesses it (Ecclesiastes 8:1); just as shamelessness, the moment its owner is seen, proves the one in whom it has made its home worthy of hatred. One must pay very careful heed to the words of the king, and avoid an oath in every way, above all one made in the name of God (Ecclesiastes 8:2). Even so, one should keep watch over an evil word, but guard against all blasphemy toward the Master (Ecclesiastes 8:3). For when he inflicts anything, there will be no finding fault, nor any speaking against the decrees of the only Sovereign and King (Ecclesiastes 8:4). It is better and more profitable to hold fast to the holy commandments and to stand clear of evil words (Ecclesiastes 8:5). For a wise man knows and foresees the judgment that comes in its time, that it will be just.

For all the affairs of human life await the punishment that comes from above (Ecclesiastes 8:6); but the wicked man does not seem to understand well that, since great providence watches over him, nothing whatever will escape notice in time to come. For he does not know what is coming, and no one will be able to declare any of it as it deserves (Ecclesiastes 8:7); for no one will be so strong as to be able to hinder the angel who takes away his soul, nor could any means at all be found to set aside the hour of death. Rather, like a man caught in the middle of a battle, one sees on every side what cannot be escaped; and all a man's ungodliness perishes with him (Ecclesiastes 8:8).
notes: Numbering is the same in English and LXX. 'Shamelessness ... worthy of hatred' follows LXX 8:1 'the shameless of face will be hated'. Doubtful sense: Ἐφίστασθαι δὲ ὅμως προσήκει λόγῳ πονηρῷ is obscure (LXX 8:3 'do not stand in an evil word'); the 1622 Latin has 'sermoni malo imminere' (Opera omnia OCR, partly damaged); the English 'keep watch over an evil word' is a cautious rendering. 'When he inflicts anything' renders the subjectless genitive absolute ἐπάγοντός τι, taken of the Master (the 1622 Latin: 'non enim de eo poenam aliquam infligente queri licebit'). 'The Master' (Δεσπότης) and 'the only Sovereign and King' are capitalized because Gregory applies them to God; 'the king' in 8:2 is left lower case. 'The only Sovereign and King' may echo 1 Timothy 6:15 (μόνος δυνάστης ... βασιλεύς); the echo is possible, not clear, so it is not cited. 'Set aside the hour of death' renders the legal term παραγράφασθαι ('to bar by a plea'). 'What cannot be escaped' renders ἄφυκτα (LXX 8:8 'there is no discharge in war').
